postTitle: Match Preview: Bolton Wanderers v County

widgetData.content:
13 years of hard work, progression and promotions come to a head on Sunday afternoon, with Stockport County just one win away from securing a return to the Championship for the first time since 2002.

This club has been on a journey like no other since we last graced the second tier of the English game. Relegations, administration and 11 years out of the Football League. Just seven years ago, County were competing in their sixth consecutive season in the National League North.

But then came the rise.

County legend Jim Gannon oversaw that important first step, with his brilliant, hard-working title-winning team of 2018/19. From the despair of Chorley away to the ecstasy of Curzon Ashton and Nuneaton - Stockport County was alive again.

Owner Mark Stott arrived with bold ambitions to return the club to the Championship within seven years. Dave Challinor has been the man to lead this incredible rise, overseeing National League and League Two title successes - and now here we are, one Wembley win away from achieving the unthinkable. No manager has ever led County to three promotions, with Dave standing on the cusp of yet more history. A return to the Championship has never been closer.

It's been a strange old season at times, with County facing plenty of adversity amidst an unprecedented injury crisis, but the Hatters have once again shown their resolve and winning mentality to secure a 3rd-place finish on the final day of the campaign.

Our play-off semi-final against Stevenage produced two of County's best displays of the campaign. Ben Osborn's 'Goal of the Season contender' at the death in the first leg earned us a first ever away win in the play-offs, and Dave Challinor's team finished the job in emphatic style back at Edgeley Park last Wednesday.

An early goal from Louie Barry set us on our way, before Kyle Wootton's sumptuous finish - his 21st goal of the campaign - killed the tie before half-time. Whilst the fans celebrated at the final whistle, focus for Dave and the team quickly switched to the final, as we look to end our recent Wembley heartache and claim the biggest prize of all.

Our Opponents:

Bolton themselves arrive at Wembley looking to avenge their defeat to Oxford United in the Play-Off Final two years ago, and return to the Championship for the first time since 2019.

Successive relegations in 2019 and 2020 amidst financial issues saw the club spend a season in the fourth tier for the first time since 1988 - a sharp decline for a proud club who previously competed in the Premier League for 11 consecutive seasons.

Promotion back to League One was achieved at the first attempt under manager Ian Evatt, with a goal from Antoni Sarcevic helping them clinch a top-three finish on the final day of the campaign.

The Trotters finished 9th in their first year back in the third tier, and have since been play-off regulars - finishing in the top six in three of the last four seasons.

A semi-final defeat to Barnsley in 2023 was followed by yet more heartache in the final a year later, as unfancied Oxford United won 2-0 to seal their place in the Championship.

Last year's campaign proved more challenging for Wanderers, with Evatt dismissed mid-way through the campaign. Former Plymouth Argyle title-winner Steven Schumacher was appointed at the end of January, but, despite a strong start, was unable to get his team over the line in the play-off race - eventually finishing in 8th.

Things have been much brighter in Schumacher's first full season in charge. Bolton broke into the play-off places for the first time in November, and have remained there ever since - albeit without ever managing to significantly close the gap on Cardiff City and Lincoln City in the top two.

This year's finalists last met on Easter Monday, playing out a typically enthralling 2-2 draw at the Toughsheet Community Stadium. Johnny Kenny gave Bolton the lead in the first half, before Adama Sidibeh struck just before the break to restore parity.

Tayo Edun's first County goal put the Hatters on course for victory after the restart, but an unfortunate late own goal from Ben Osborn ensured the points were shared.

That result left Bolton in 4th, three points and one place above County having played a game more. They won just one of their remaining five games after that meeting, but that result - a 5-1 win against Stevenage - was enough to all but secure a play-off spot.

They went into the final day with a top-six finish confirmed, and were in the driving seat to claim 3rd place before a 3-2 defeat at home to Luton Town saw County leapfrog them - setting up a play-off meeting with Bradford City in the semi-finals.

Star man Amario Cozier-Duberry, on loan from Brighton, stole the headlines in the first leg at home, scoring the winner with a trademark finish bent into the far corner after cutting in from the right-hand side.

Heading back to a vociferous Valley Parade for the second leg, Schumacher's side had to withstand heavy Bradford pressure in the second half, and were indebted to goalkeeper Jack Bonham for two outstanding saves to keep the home side at bay.

Then, with nine minutes to go, Bolton broke away at speed, with substitute Xavier Simons firing home superbly from 15 yards to all but confirm Bolton's place in the final.

It's all set up for a mouth-watering meeting at Wembley on Sunday afternoon, between two sides who have become accustomed to success in recent years. It's winner takes all, with Championship football within touching distance.

Match Stats:

  • Sunday's final will be the 33rd competitive meeting between the two clubs, and the first at Wembley. County hold a narrow historical advantage, winning 12 of those previous encounters to Bolton's 11.
  • County have lost just one of the last eight meetings between the two sides - a 2-0 defeat in the Vertu Trophy in 2023.
  • This will be County's eighth trip to Wembley, with the Hatters looking for their second win under the arch.
  • If selected, Ollie Norwood will make his 50th appearance of the season on Sunday - and his 99th for the club since signing in 2024.
